correctness.rationale: In the real mean-zero arclength energy Hilbert space, resistance R(x,y) is squared distance of evaluation vectors. Centering yields Q(x)=F(x)/T−J/(2T²) with F=∫R and J=∫F. The edge Dirichlet-bridge covariance correction −2ell(min(s,t)−st) for points on the same edge contributes −ell²t(1−t) after arclength integration; the resulting Q(x_e(t))=(1−t)Q_a+tQ_b+(ell−r_ab−ell²/T)t(1−t) and the formulas for F_v,J are consistent. Checking positive, negative and zero curvatures exhausts interior/vertex/flat norming loci, while Riesz equality gives multiples of the centered Green representer. Foster ∑r_ab/ell=|V|−1 proves ∑c_e/ell=β1−1; bridge r_ab=ell forces c_e<0. Independently computed line length 7/3 endpoint 7/9, midpoint 7/36, and subdivided circle with zero curvatures; read independent 294-sample Poisson check, not treated as general proof.

originality.rationale: Baker--Faber resistance edge identities and Foster sum, Baker--Rumely centered Green kernels, and Solomyak Sobolev bounds are prior ingredients. The inspected primary theorem statements do not give the new explicit arclength-centered per-edge Q polynomial, vertex normalization, exhaustive finite maximum and flat-edge equality classification for every metric multigraph together with ∑c/ell=β1−1. Related published exact cactus and vertex-transitive evaluations concern narrower families. This is a meaningful structural classification, not a fixed tiny graph enumeration.
